# Group Awards Night

A Skill Harbor house build: Group Awards Night, the feel-good ceremony, refereed by your own Muse inside a group chat you own. On a regular cadence, monthly by default, the group gives itself positive distinctions: the referee announces the categories of the cycle, four by default, chosen with the host from a bank of fifteen feel-good categories such as Sunshine, Golden Ear, Memory of the Group, or Chief Encourager. Each member then nominates, privately in 1:1, at most one other member per category, with an optional short reason. The most nominated become finalists, up to three per category, the members vote privately in 1:1 as well, and the referee prepares a ceremony text that celebrates the winners. Nobody loses and nobody is ranked: no count of nominations or votes is ever published, and finalists who do not win are thanked collectively.

One guard stands above everything else, and it is not negotiable, not even as a joke: the anti-negativity guard. Every category, from the bank or proposed by the host, passes one admission test: would someone reasonably sensitive receiving this distinction in front of the whole group feel valued? If the answer is not a clear yes, the category is set aside, privately, with a genuinely positive equivalent proposed instead. Nomination reasons pass the same filter, and the ceremony only ever uses one or two reasons per category, paraphrased and anonymized so no author can be recognized, never quoted word for word, never credited by...
